title: Bidirectional A* in Cape Town: Meet-in-the-Middle!
description: Watch Bidirectional A* slice through a real street graph by expanding simultaneously from start and goal. The fronts “meet in the middle,” cutting search work while keeping A*’s best-first efficiency.
ig_caption:
🚦✨ **Bidirectional A*** on real streets in **Cape Town (Gardens)**

When you run **Bidirectional A***, you don’t expand from just one side—you grow **two A*-guided frontiers**: one from the **start node** and another from the **goal node**. Each frontier uses a **heuristic** (like distance-to-target) to prioritize promising streets, while the search space shrinks dramatically once the paths **intersect**. 🧠📍

On a real city map, we model intersections/road segments as a **graph** (nodes + weighted edges). Then the algorithm becomes a fast **graph search** problem: it explores fewer edges than classic A* by coordinating both directions and stopping when the combined route is guaranteed optimal (given admissible/consistent heuristics). 🗺️⚙️
